eyebrow: Advanced SRE, Disaster Recovery & Resilience · Chapter 2
subtitle: Lesson 1 · Advanced Incident Management

steps.label: Incident Commander
steps.sub: Owns the incident as a process — assigns work, decides on escalation, never debugs personally

steps.label: Communications Lead
steps.sub: Single voice for anything leaving the incident channel, on a fixed update cadence

steps.label: Scribe
steps.sub: Keeps a live, timestamped timeline — the postmortem's primary source later

code:
14:02  Alerts fire: p99 latency > 2s on checkout-api

14:06  Platform team joins; LB error rate confirmed elevated
14:09  DB team joins; replication lag confirmed at 40s
14:15  Hypothesis: bad migration at 13:58 — rollback requested
14:19  Rollback complete; error rate recovering
14:27  Error rate back to baseline
14:45  IC declares incident resolved
caption: A live, timestamped log — not a reconstruction written days later from memory.

steps.label: SEV3, one team, ten minutes
steps.sub: On-call engineer handles it solo, no IC structure needed

steps.label: Crosses team boundaries
steps.sub: IC, Communications Lead, and Scribe are staffed

steps.label: Major, long-running incident
steps.sub: A Deputy IC may take over so the primary IC can rest

subtitle: One channel, clear ownership, no team debugging in the dark.
